title: A finished workout can quietly skip Health Connect when the sample-data check fails
what: Before sending a workout to Health Connect the app asks whether the phone holds sample data. If that question itself fails (a passing database hiccup the app already knows about), the answer is taken as 'yes, sample data': the real workout is not sent, nothing is written to the log, and it is taken off the 'Send again' list. The member's Health Connect simply misses that workout and the page never says so. 'Send past workouts' can also wrongly treat the history as sample data.
expected: A failed check is treated as a failed send: the workout stays on the 'Send again' list and the failure is logged, so the member sees 'didn't reach Health Connect' and can retry.
fix_line: When the sample-data check fails, keep the workout for Send again and log it instead of calling it sample data

title: When the home-screen widgets cannot be updated they keep old facts and nothing records why
what: Every widget update after a save, a delete, or a started or ended workout swallows any failure with no log line at all, and the phone's own 'save failed' answer is ignored. The 'Today' widget can keep offering 'Resume' for a finished workout or show yesterday's routine, the week widget can miss a day trained, and the app-icon shortcuts stay old. Neither the member nor MettleUp ever learns that the update failed.
expected: A failed widget update is at least written to the log (and to the crash reports that reach MettleUp), and the next app opening tries again.
fix_line: Log every failed widget update and act on the phone's save-failed answer

title: If the phone refuses the rest timer's alarm, 'Rest is over' can come late or not at all with the app closed, and nothing records it
what: When a rest starts, the phone sets an alarm so 'Rest is over' rings even with MettleUp closed or the screen off. If the precise alarm is refused, the code quietly drops to a looser alarm that Android may hold back for minutes; if every kind is refused, no alarm is set at all. None of these steps writes a log line or tells the member, so a late or missing rest alert cannot be traced afterwards. The alert check-up only looks at the permission, not at whether the alarm was really set.
expected: Each downgrade (precise to loose, or no alarm) is logged, and a rest with no alarm at all tells the member to keep the app open.
fix_line: Log each alarm downgrade and warn the member when no alarm could be set

title: Sharing a Hevy or Strong export to MettleUp can do nothing, with no message
what: When a member shares an export file to MettleUp from Android's share menu, the app reads the file from the phone side. If that read fails in an unexpected way, the failure is swallowed: the import screen never opens, no message appears and nothing is logged. Only 'too big' and 'unreadable' answers reach the member.
expected: Any failure to take the shared file opens the import screen with a plain 'could not read this file' message.
fix_line: Show the unreadable-file message for any failed read of a shared file
